name: Easy Interview
tagline: AI-assisted interview tooling for screening candidates: generate questions, collect answers, get summaries and scores.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core here is genuinely a weekend build: take a job description, have an LLM produce structured questions, record or type candidate answers, transcribe, score against a rubric, dump a summary. None of that needs proprietary data or a network. What you do not get in one session is the part that faces strangers: a candidate link that works on a five year old Android in a hotel wifi dead zone, video that uploads reliably, email that lands, and a record you would be comfortable showing a lawyer. Hiring tools also carry real legal weight in a way personal tools do not, since automated screening decisions are regulated in several jurisdictions and 'my AI ranked them' is a bad answer in a discrimination claim. Build it if you are screening for your own small team and reading every transcript yourself; buy something if candidates outside your building are going to touch it.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that turns a job description into a structured question set, collects candidate answers by text or browser recording, transcribes them, and scores each answer against a rubric with an LLM.
requirements: An LLM API key in .env, or a local model if you prefer
Whisper (API or whisper.cpp) for transcription if you accept audio or video
A publicly reachable URL if candidates outside your machine need to respond: a small VPS or a tunnel
Disk or object storage for recordings, they get large fast
Somewhere to send invite links from, your own inbox is fine at low volume
whatYouLose: Candidate-side reliability: device permissions, upload retries, mobile browsers, timezone handling, all the boring stuff that decides whether you actually get the interview
Scoring that has been calibrated across thousands of interviews rather than whatever your rubric prompt happened to say on Tuesday
ATS, calendar and email integrations, so results live in your app instead of the pipeline your recruiters use
An audit trail and a vendor who has thought about EEOC, GDPR and EU AI Act exposure on automated candidate assessment
Anti-cheat and identity signals, which matter more every month that answer-generating AI gets better
moatNotes: The moat is not the prompt. It is being the party that signs off on a screening process someone might sue over, plus making the candidate-facing flow not break.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is not optimizing for cost, they are optimizing for not being embarrassed. A hiring manager will happily pay a monthly fee so that fifty candidates get a link that works, so scores look consistent enough to defend in a debrief, and so the results land in the ATS instead of a folder on someone's laptop. Your self-hosted version handles the interesting 80 percent and leaves you personally responsible for the 20 percent that involves strangers, lawyers and deliverability. That trade is fine for a founder screening ten people and terrible for a recruiting team screening a thousand.
notes: Fine as an internal screening helper for a team you can shout across; stop short of letting it make the decision.
prompt:
Build a local-first interview screening tool called "deskinterview". No hosted accounts, no telemetry, single operator.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with server actions
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, migrations in ./migrations run on boot
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- LLM calls through the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API, base URL and key from .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, MODEL)
- Transcription via the same provider's audio transcription endpoint, key from .env
- Recordings written to ./data/media on local disk, never to a third party

In scope:
1. Roles: create a role with a title and a pasted job description. One click generates 5 to 8 structured interview questions plus a per-question scoring rubric (1 to 5, with what each level looks like). Questions and rubric are editable and versioned, and the version used is stored on every interview.
2. Candidates: add name and email, generate an unguessable invite link (random 32 char token) per candidate per role. Links expire after a configurable number of days.
3. Candidate page at /i/[token]: shows one question at a time, accepts either a typed answer or a browser MediaRecorder audio recording, saves progress after each question, works without login. Handle denied mic permission by falling back to text.
4. Processing: on submit, transcribe any audio, then score each answer against its rubric with the LLM. Store the raw model output, the parsed score, and a two sentence justification per question. Never store a hire/no-hire recommendation.
5. Operator dashboard: list candidates per role, per-question scores, transcripts, audio playback, and a compare view across candidates for the same role. Export a role's results as CSV and JSON.
6. Every scored answer displays a visible "AI draft, human decides" banner and requires the operator to enter their own score before the candidate can be marked reviewed.

Out of scope, do not build: video recording, calendar or ATS integrations, payment, multi-tenant orgs, email sending (generate links for the operator to copy), anti-cheat detection, auto-ranking or auto-rejection.

Requirements: seed script with one example role and two fake candidates, .env.example with every key, README covering setup, where data lives, how to delete a candidate and all their media, and a short honest note that automated candidate assessment is regulated in some jurisdictions and this tool keeps a human in the loop on purpose. Basic HTTP auth on everything except /i/[token], credentials from .env.
